items.q: Count in 5s: 20, 25, 30. What number comes next?
items.hint: Count on 5 more with one hand: 31, 32, 33, 34, 35.

slips.say: 31 is only 1 more. Counting in 5s, the jump is 5.
40 is 10 more. Counting in 5s, the jump is 5.

tpl.q: Count in 5s: {s}, {a}, {b}. What number comes next?

items.q: Count in 10s: 13, 23, 33. What number comes next?
items.hint: Ten more is one row down on the 100 square.

slips.say: 34 is only 1 more. Counting in 10s, the jump is 10.
53 is 20 more. One jump is 10.

tpl.q: Count in 10s: {s}, {a}, {b}. What number comes next?
tpl.hint: Ten more is one row down on the 100 square.

items.q: A counter is on 34 on the 100 square. The counter moves down 1 square. Which number is it on?
steps: One step down is one row.
A row has ten squares, so down is 10 more.

slips.say: 35 is one square to the right. We moved down, which is 10 more.
24 is one square up. We moved down, so add 10.

tpl.q: A counter is on {n} on the 100 square. The counter moves down 1 square. Which number is it on?
steps: One step down is one row.
A row has ten squares, so down is 10 more.

items.q: A counter is on 52 on the 100 square. The counter moves right 1 square. Which number is it on?

slips.say: 62 is one row down. We moved right, which is 1 more.
51 is one square to the left.

tpl.q: A counter is on {n} on the 100 square. The counter moves right 1 square. Which number is it on?

items.q: Count in 2s: 6, 8, 10. What number comes next?

slips.say: 11 is only 1 more. Counting in 2s, the jump is 2.

tpl.q: Count in 2s: {s}, {a}, {b}. What number comes next?

items.q: Which number do you say when you count in 5s from 5?
items.hint: Numbers counted in 5s end in 5 or 0.

slips.say: 32 ends in 2. Counting in 5s, the last digit is 5 or 0.

items.q: On the 100 square, a counter is on 8. The counter moves down 3 rows. What number is it on at the end?
items.hint: One row down is 10 more. Three rows are 30 more.

slips.say: 11 is only 3 more. Each row down is 10 more, so 3 rows is 30 more.
30 is the number of squares moved. Start from 8.

tpl.q: On the 100 square, a counter is on {n}. The counter moves down {r} rows. What number is it on at the end?
tpl.hint: One row down is 10 more. {r} rows are {m} more.

items.q: Look at the pattern: 3, 4, 6, 9, __. The gaps grow by 1 each time. What number comes next?
items.hint: The gaps are 1, 2, 3. What is the next gap?

slips.say: 12 adds 3 again. The gap must grow by 1, so the next gap is 4.
10 adds 1. The gaps grow: 1, 2, 3, then 4.

tpl.q: Look at the pattern: {s}, {b}, {c}, {d}, __. The gaps grow by 1 each time. What number comes next?
tpl.hint: The gaps are 1, 2, 3. What is the next gap?

items.q: Mei counts in 2s from 2 up to 30. Ali counts in 5s from 5 up to 30. How many numbers do they both say?
items.hint: List both. Which numbers are in both lists?
steps: Mei says the numbers ending in 0, 2, 4, 6, 8. Ali says the numbers ending in 5 or 0.

slips.say: There are more than one. Keep looking for numbers in both lists: 10, then?
6 is how many numbers Ali says. Count only the numbers in both lists.

tpl.q: Mei counts in 2s from 2 up to {N}. Ali counts in 5s from 5 up to {N}. How many numbers do they both say?
tpl.hint: List both. Which numbers are in both lists?
steps: Mei says the numbers ending in 0, 2, 4, 6, 8. Ali says the numbers ending in 5 or 0.
The numbers in both lists end in 0.
They both say {ans} numbers up to {N}.

items.q: Which pattern has gaps that grow?
items.hint: Find the gap between each pair of numbers.
steps: The other lists have gaps that stay the same or get smaller.
So 3, 4, 6, 9 is the pattern with growing gaps.

slips.say: That one always adds 3, so the gap stays the same.

items.q: Look at this chain: 1, 4, 5, 9, 14, __. After 1 and 4, each number is the last two numbers added together. What comes next?
items.hint: Add the last two numbers: 9 and 14.

slips.say: 19 is 14 and 5 added. Add the two numbers just before: 9 and 14.
28 is 14 + 14. Add the last two numbers 9 and 14.

tpl.q: Look at this chain: {a}, {b}, {c}, {d}, {e}, __. After {a} and {b}, each number is the last two numbers added together. What comes next?
tpl.hint: Add the last two numbers: {d} and {e}.

items.q: Two patterns are mixed in one list: 5, 50, 10, 45, 15, 40, __. What number comes next?
items.hint: Look at every second number. Which rule comes next?
steps: The 1st, 3rd and 5th numbers are 5, 10, 15: they go up by 5.
The next one in that rule is 20.

slips.say: 35 is the number after next. The next number follows the first rule: 5, 10, 15, then?
45 is already in the list. Check which rule comes next.

items.q: Look at a block of 4 squares on the 100 square. 34 and 35 are on top. 44 and 45 are below. Add 34 and 45. What is the total?
items.hint: Add the top left number and the bottom right number.
steps: The top left number is 34 and the bottom right is 45.

slips.say: 69 is 34 + 35. Add the top left (34) and the bottom right (45).

tpl.q: Look at a block of 4 squares on the 100 square. {a} and {b} are on top. {c} and {d} are below. Add {a} and {d}. What is the total?
tpl.hint: Add the top left number and the bottom right number.
steps: The top left number is {a} and the bottom right is {d}.
The other slant, {b} + {c}, makes the same total.

items.q: Hide a number on the 100 square. Write 3 clues for your grown-up. For example: you say it when you count in 5s; it is more than 40; it is less than 50. Check that only ONE number fits.
items.hint: Pick a secret number first. Then write clues that are true for it.
steps: Check your secret number fits every clue.
List the numbers that fit the first clue. Cross out any that break clue 2 or clue 3.
Exactly one number should be left. For example: counting in 5s, more than 40 and less than 50 leaves only 45.
